text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwe's Matabeleland Zambezi Water Project, aiming to build a 450-km water pipeline from the Zambezi river to arid Matabeleland province border, is close to being realised after the Arab Fund for Economic Development in Africa promised to fund it to the tune of Z$7 billion. Details of the provisional loan agreement are not available.

- Harare's executive mayor Solomon Tawenga has refused to sanction a Z$20 million project signed between the Harare City Council officials and a Lebanese company, El Nour United Engineering Group, to develop a shopping complex, which was reached without going through a tender process.
- More young Zimbabweans must go into agriculture and mining with government support to help sustain economic development in Zimbabwe, President Robert Mugabe told the Herald.
- Mugabe told a conference of his ruling ZANU-PF party that unity holds the key to achievement of all Zimbabwe's political, economic and social aspirations.
